explanation: The king of Persia who allowed the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.
The capital city of ancient Israel and Judah, a central place for Jewish faith and culture.
A holy place in Jerusalem where the Jews worshipped God and performed religious ceremonies.
The king of Babylon who conquered Jerusalem, destroyed the temple, and led the Jews into exile.
A period when the Jews were forced to leave their homeland and live in foreign lands, especially Babylon.
A righteous king of Judah who sought to reform the kingdom and lead the people back to God.
The southern kingdom of the two Israelite kingdoms, consisting of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
The last king of Judah, installed by Nebuchadnezzar but later rebelled against him.
A person who received messages from God and delivered them to the people; often prophets warned about the consequences of disobedience to God.
